steps.title: A shared map
steps.body: Almost every rule in football is about ==where the ball is==. The field gives players, refs and fans the same map, so a gain of 7 means the same thing to everyone.

steps.title: 100 yards, two end zones
steps.body: The field is ==100 yards== from goal line to goal line, with a ==10-yard end zone== at each end. It's 53⅓ yards wide, with a line every 5 yards to measure progress.

steps.title: Feet in
steps.body: In pro football a catch near the sideline only counts if the receiver gets ==both feet down inbounds== with control of the ball. The white sideline itself is ==out==.

steps.title: The hash marks
steps.body: When a play ends near the sideline, the ball comes back to the nearest ==hash mark== for the next snap, so the offense always has room on both sides.

steps.title: Breaking the plane
steps.body: A touchdown counts the moment ==the ball crosses the goal line== in a runner's control. His feet can still be outside the end zone.
steps.note: Ref signal: both arms straight up.

steps.title: Out of bounds
steps.body: Stepping out isn't a penalty, but it ==ends the play== on the spot. Late in a half, runners head for the sideline on purpose, because going out of bounds ==stops the clock==.

steps.prompt: Why was the pass ruled incomplete?
options: His foot came down out of bounds
steps.explain: He caught it cleanly, but his second foot landed on the sideline. The line counts as out, so the pass is incomplete.

steps.prompt: How long is the field from goal line to goal line?
steps.explain: 100 yards between the goal lines. Add the two 10-yard end zones and the whole field is 120.
